notes:
**Your journal was counting trades that lost money as wins.** Win rate, profit factor, average win, average loss - all of it came from the difference between two prices with the charges thrown away. A scratch that made twenty rupees and paid forty was a win. The trades most likely to flip sign once costs are counted are exactly the small quick ones a journal is full of, so the scoreboard flattered precisely the habit this app exists to warn you about.

**The coach was doing the same thing.** Every observation it makes about money - your risk-reward, your win rate, your loss streaks - read gross P&L. A scalper whose trades made forty rupees and cost sixty was told he had good discipline.

**An expired commodity contract now says so** instead of reporting that your broker will not serve its candles.

*If you skipped 0.9.82: an option's stop was booked against the index's price, deployed rules were not paying the spread, and every greek depended on your phone's timezone.*
